title: Dealing With Surprising Human Emotions: Desk Moves

summary: “Desk moves are my favorite example of why managers should understand the brain science behind why people react they way they do, in otherwise not-that-emotional circumstances.”

title: Engineering Management After The Cost Of Code Collapsed
author: Karim Jedda
summary: “I still hear and read what I call the “old rules” repeated over and over: a director should not spend time coding, good work takes time, protect the team from the business, get consensus before you commit, etc...” Karim started checking each rule against the assumption underneath it.

title: The Conductor Developer

title: My Agentic Coding Setup, July 2026
author: Domenic Denicola
summary: “Things are changing very fast, and I have no illusions that this will be a timeless nugget of wisdom. But talking to some friends and scrolling through X posts, it does seem that I might have some techniques in play that are not widespread.”

title: How Miro Builds And Tests Agentic Features At Scale
summary: Miro's AI team was building a new AI architecture across nearly 250 microservices, and one shared environment meant tests constantly collided. With Signadot, they moved to verifying changes in parallel with lightweight environments in the cluster.

title: Work Loudly
author: Ben Balter
summary: “In remote work, visibility isn't ambient anymore. If your work only shows up at the end - or only in your head and DMs—you make it harder for people to help, harder for managers to advocate for you, and easier for the org to miss your impact.”

title: The Bedrock of Software Design
author: Alex Fedoseev
summary: “Nothing has influenced the way I design software more than algebraic data types. It sounds overly academic—the kind of term that makes people roll their eyes or scares them away altogether. But honestly, it only sounds scary.”

title: Every Byte Matters
author: Farid Zakaria
summary: Farid argues that classic analysis isn't enough. The size of your data matters as much as your algorithm. CPUs pull memory in 64-byte cache lines, so how tightly your data packs into those lines impacts speed.

title: Before You Delegate, Ask Yourself These 6 Questions
author: Wes Kao
summary: (1) What does this person know? What’s new for them? (2) Why are we doing this? (3) What do they need in order to do this task? (4) What does great look like? (5) What’s the timeline and priority level? (6) What’s most likely to go wrong?

title: The Big Management Lie: Overpromising
summary: “When managers are under pressure, and especially when they’re under pressure to retain a high performer, overpromising is one of the most common tools to reach for. The industry is rife with promises that someone will get a promotion, a new role, a large bonus.”

title: Gauntlet AI Night School — On Demand: Watch Every Session, Free

title: Yes You Can Measure Engineering

title: How To Write An Effective Software Design Document
author: Michael Lynch

title: Relentless Forward Progress
author: Mike Fisher
summary: “The hardest stretches of running a team are not sprints. They are ultras: the long downturn, the slow turnaround, the market that stays bad for six quarters straight. None is solved by a single heroic burst. They are survived, or not, by how you manage the long middle.”

title: The Antithesis Principle
author: Shreyas Doshi
summary: (1) If you want to help people learn something, look into making it engaging / entertaining. This first one is the easier, more obvious conclusion. (2) It is actually not in your best interest to be the kind of person who can only learn from entertaining content.

title: A Practical Guide To Rapid Onboarding
author: Steve Huynh

title: Agentic Code Quality
